note: Links that the other sources of scripts/build-vessel-parents.mjs do not carry: the continuations of the main trunks (aorta, subclavian→axillary, brachiocephalic veins, leg veins) and the brachial plexus and sciatic nerve trees. `%` is Right/Left (lower-case inside a name), `.s` the nerve-stream suffix .r/.l; `why` is the textbook fact each link states (Gray's Anatomy 1918; OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology). The builder fails when a name is not a structure of the model.

links.why: The subclavian artery becomes the axillary artery at the lateral border of the first rib.
The aortic arch continues as the descending thoracic aorta.
The thoracic aorta passes through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm and becomes the abdominal aorta.
The abdominal aorta divides into the two common iliac arteries.
The celiac trunk is the first unpaired branch of the abdominal aorta.
The superior mesenteric artery arises from the abdominal aorta below the celiac trunk.
The inferior mesenteric artery arises from the abdominal aorta below the renal arteries.
The renal arteries arise from the sides of the abdominal aorta.
The axillary vein becomes the subclavian vein at the lateral border of the first rib.
The subclavian vein joins the internal jugular vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.
The brachiocephalic veins unite to form the superior vena cava.
The brachiocephalic veins unite to form the superior vena cava.
The azygos vein arches over the right main bronchus and drains into the superior vena cava.
The hemiazygos vein crosses the vertebral column and drains into the azygos vein.
The accessory hemiazygos vein crosses the vertebral column and drains into the azygos vein.
The internal thoracic vein drains into the brachiocephalic vein.
The small saphenous vein drains into the popliteal vein.
The great saphenous vein drains into the femoral vein at the saphenous opening.
The popliteal vein continues as the femoral vein.
The femoral vein continues as the external iliac vein behind the inguinal ligament.
The external and internal iliac veins unite to form the common iliac vein.
The external and internal iliac veins unite to form the common iliac vein.
The two common iliac veins unite to form the inferior vena cava.
The renal veins drain into the inferior vena cava.
The superficial epigastric vein drains into the great saphenous vein.
The inferior epigastric vein drains into the external iliac vein.
